title: finding(types): two published zod mirrors validate a key their TypeScript twin never declares (`dueLike`, `operators`) — and the third the ledger groups with them is a tombstone that REFUSES, not a mirror that admits
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat, session `session_01UanLVj6xvbS6puBCewLr8L`, R1. ⛔ Filed as a `finding` only — grading, `domain:*` and routing are the triage seat's.

## The shape

PR objectui#9725 (card objectui#9711) landed the fourth parity direction — `MirroredUndeclaredKeys`, a key the **zod mirror declares** and the **TypeScript twin does not**. Its seeded ledger names **8 entries / 102 keys**, a FLOOR that can only shrink. This card carries the three **LOCAL, single-key** entries, which are the ones with a concrete per-key answer.

⚠️ ⛔ **And it corrects the hand-back that produced it: the three do NOT behave the same way.** Two are silent-green; the third is the opposite.

| pair | key | the mirror's shape on `origin/main` | what an author who writes the key gets |
|---|---|---|---|
| `views.zod.ts#DetailViewFieldSchema` | `dueLike` (`:86`) | `z.boolean(` — **live mirror** | ✅ a **green** `safeParse` from a published validator for a key the published types never invited |
| `objectql.zod.ts#ObjectGridSchema` | `operators` (`:283`) | `z.record(` — **live mirror** | same |
| `complex.zod.ts#DashboardConfigSchema` | `aria` (`:1239`) | **`z.never(`** — a `retirementTombstone` carrying 「RETIRED (objectui#5852)」 | ⛔ a **RED** parse, by name, with a remedy |

⇒ the third is ⛔ **not** the same defect. The operator reports it because a tombstone is still a declared member of the zod shape while the TypeScript face has nothing — but its consequence is the **opposite**: it refuses the key rather than silently admitting it. ⭐ Grouping it with the other two would ask a maintainer to fix something that is already doing its job.

## Why the two live ones are a contract defect

Both published faces ship together from `@object-ui/types`, and they disagree about the accept set: the validator says yes, the type says nothing. An author following the types never writes the key; an author who guesses it gets a green parse and no type. ⛔ Neither face is obviously the wrong one — that is what makes it a ruling and not a repair.

## ⚠️ How this seat got it wrong twice before getting it right — the reading that matters

The hand-back said `dueLike` appears 「nowhere in this package's TypeScript declarations」. Checking that produced **two false readings in a row**, and the second is the instructive one:

1. **Dark instrument.** A `git grep` with pathspec `packages/types/src/**/*.ts` plus `:!` exclusions returned **0** for `cardTitle` — a key independently verified as declared at `objectql.ts:3786`. ⛔ Two zeros on one instrument is a broken instrument; the reading was voided, ⛔ not reported. Re-drawn against an **enumerated file list** (44 non-zod, non-test `.ts`), the control lit: `cardTitle` → 1, `collapsed` → 4, absent control → 0.

2. ⭐ **Then the lit instrument said `dueLike` → 2 and `operators` → 2, and it was STILL the wrong question.** Located:

   | key | found at | owning interface |
   |---|---|---|
   | `dueLike` | `field-types.ts:455`, `:481` | ⛔ **not** the `DetailViewField` twin |
   | `operators` | `complex.ts:720` (`FilterBuilderOperator[]`), `data-protocol.ts:656` (`AdvancedFilterOperator[]`) | ⛔ **not** `ObjectGridSchema` |

   ⇒ neither is declared on **its own pair's twin**, which is what the operator measures. The hand-back was right; my probe asked 「is this NAME anywhere in the package's TypeScript?」 when the question is 「is this KEY on THIS pair's twin?」.

⭐ **A name is not a key. A key is (interface, name).** A lit control certifies that the instrument can see declarations; it says nothing about whether the instrument is scoped to the right declaration. That is the same class as this board's standing rule — a lit control certifies the INSTRUMENT, not the QUESTION — reaching a third distinct shape today.

## What a taker must decide, per key

Declare it on the twin (**enlarges** the TypeScript accept set) or narrow the mirror (**shrinks** the validator's). Both move a published face ⇒ **`Clause-②: yes`** and an at-tier contract review. ⛔ Neither is a mechanical edit, which is why this is a card and not a sweep.

⚠️ `operators` carries its own provenance and it is this family's thesis in one key: the mirror's line is annotated 「Missing in previous TS scan but common」 — the gap was **noticed by a human at authoring time, written into a comment, and then measured by nothing** until the fourth direction existed.

## What this card does NOT carry

⛔ The five **SPEC-DERIVED** entries (42 keys across `app.zod.ts#AppComponentSchema`, `complex.zod.ts#DashboardComponentSchema`, `layout.zod.ts#PageNodeSchema`, `objectql.zod.ts#ObjectGridSchema`) — those mirror the spec surface **by reference** while the hand-written interface restates only the subset renderers read. Different mechanism, different remedy, a spec-alignment axis. To be filed separately.

⛔ The **`Omit` collapse** class (`form.zod.ts#InputShorthandSchema`, `#UiCalendarSchema`) — `Exclude< keyof Base, K >` resolving through `string` when `Base` carries `BaseSchema`'s index signature. Both live instances are ⭐ already documented in `packages/types/src/form.ts` and pinned per key by `content-channel-family-d-9256.test.ts`; what is ungated is the **class**, not a live victim.

## Dedup terms

`mirrored-but-undeclared` · `MirroredUndeclared ledger` · `dueLike` · `operators` · `zod-only published key`

## Provenance

Handed back by the implementer of objectui#9711 (PR objectui#9725) as out of that card's scope — correctly, since remedying any of them moves a published accept set, which its dispatch forbade. Every row above was re-derived by this seat on `origin/main`; the `aria` correction and the (interface, name) reading are ⛔ **not** in the hand-back.
